title: The Midnight Hollow Anew
premise: Wren Okafor has survived two decades in the city of Vell by hiding his gift behind harmless charms, until the crown's witch-hunt forces him to flee with a found family of other marked souls. Their escape route lies through the Midnight Hollow, the unmapped realm Wren alone can chart, but the court beneath the mountain holds the soul of his young ward, Tamsin, sold years ago by her desperate mother to buy her safety. To reclaim it, Wren must trade his own name from the world's memory, erasing himself from every map and mind that knows him. He succeeds, but at the cost of being forgotten by the very family he saved, until Tamsin, now keeper of his maps, teaches them all to remember him anew.
about_author: Elodie Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing explorers' maps before turning to fiction about the places they feared to draw. She writes fantasy about people who belong nowhere until they build somewhere together.

chapters.title: The Color of Ash
chapters.summary: In Wren's POV, the crown's heralds nail the Proscription to Vell's gates, and his neighbor is dragged away for a charm no larger than a button. Wren burns his charm-stock, gathers his ragtag household, and discovers Tamsin's soul-mark glowing on her wrist: proof of the old bargain. The beat is fear hardening into resolve as he chooses flight over invisibility.

chapters.title: What the Maps Refuse
chapters.summary: The fugitives enter the Hollow, where terrain shifts to mock memory, and only Wren's cartography can hold a path. Tamsin's POV reveals she overheard the terms of her soul-sale and resents being protected from the truth. When a companion is nearly lost to a shifting pass, Wren confesses everything; the beat is loyalty strained by secrets, then tempered by honesty.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Descending into the mountain court, Wren bargains with the Pale Registrar, who offers Tamsin's soul for Wren's name, his existence struck from every memory and record. In the Registrar's POV we see its loneliness and hunger for a name freely given. Wren accepts; the climax lands as he signs away himself while his family sleeps, unaware.

chapters.title: Anew
chapters.summary: Tamsin wakes whole but finds a stranger tending their fire, a man her family cannot remember yet her soul recognizes. Using Wren's own maps, annotated in his hand across twenty years, she retraces their shared history aloud until the others begin to recall him piece by piece. The resolution beats with belonging rebuilt deliberately: memory as an act of love, not inheritance.
